subject: MAP: BrightHealth evaluation cadence and decision cascade — proposed backstop
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-07-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: BrightHealth MAP: evaluation cadence + decision cascade — potential close drift

Team,

Quick heads-up: BrightHealth's procurement paused the PO sign-off earlier today pending a final data-retention attestation and SOC-2 evidence. That puts our previously agreed close (7/22) at risk — procurement has flagged a 7–10 business day internal review if we can't surface the attestation this week.

Impacts I've identified:
- Eval window (MAP milestone 2) will slip, which cascades acceptance and billing.
- If we miss the go/no-go date, they will push acceptance into a single gate vs. phased (bigger risk to our revenue recognition).
- Procurement may require a credit for missed SLAs or an escrow-style acceptance.

Immediate asks:
1) Karthik — can you confirm what SOC-2 artifacts we can surface by EOD Thursday? If there are any gaps, enumerate them and estimate days to close.
2) Laura — build two rebaseline options (A: minimal slip with contingency credits; B: staged acceptance with extended eval window). Keep asks tight and prescriptive.
3) Jordan — if we need to loop legal, prep a short contract amendment template that supports either option and a ~14-day extension.

I want a one-pager by Thu morning so I can align with Alex before his next procurement sync. We should propose a clear backstop (staged acceptance or credit) rather than handing them open-ended timeline flexibility.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0132

Attachment: internal_risk_notes_stub.txt (see internal summary)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Green <alex.green@brighthealth.com>, Procurement Team <procure@brighthealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-07-12T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: RE: MAP v3 + evaluation schedule — proposed options to avoid close drift

Alex / Procurement,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our conversation I've attached the current MAP (v3) and two narrowly scoped proposals to keep you moving without losing momentum on acceptance:

Option 1 — Short extension + contingency credits (preferred):
- Extend decision date from 2029-07-22 to 2029-08-05 (14 calendar days).
- Maintain current milestone gating; if acceptance slips beyond 8/05 without remediation, we agree to a one-time credit (X% of month 1 invoice) or 30-day usage credit.

Option 2 — Staged acceptance (partial in prod for core slice):
- Allow early go-live for a defined scope (Prod Slice A) by 7/22, full acceptance by 8/19.
- Shared acceptance criteria for Slice A in attached MAP.

What we need from BrightHealth this week:
- Clear indication which option you prefer by EOD Thursday (7/18).
- If Option 1, a procurement hold-lift timeline for the attestation so we can prepare billing and cutover.
- If Option 2, confirmation of the Prod Slice A owner and a quick sign-off on the acceptance checklist.

Attachments: BrightHealth_MAP_v3.xlsx (MAP with milestone dates and gating), SOW redline summary (see inline notes).

I'll loop Jordan and legal if we get a preference so we can push a contract amendment for signatures. We want to avoid open-ended extensions — the backstop is either the credit or staged acceptance.

Best,
Vanessa
Senior Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
Vanessa Ortiz

Vanessa / Laura — looping legal and external counsel for visibility. Sarah, attaching a concise amendment that supports either Option 1 (14-day extension + credit) or Option 2 (staged acceptance). Key points:

- Amendment must not change core scope or pricing, only the acceptance timeline and the limited credit trigger.

- Limit credit exposure: one-time credit capped at 10% of month 1 ARR and applied only if acceptance is not achieved by the agreed backstop date.
- Include an expedited evidence exchange clause: BrightHealth provides attestation artifacts within X business days and Redwood provides required SOC excerpts within Y business days.

Alex / Team,

Thanks for the fast turnaround. Per Alex's note and our internal review, BrightHealth and Redwood have agreed on the following rebaseline and backstop (summarized):

1) Rebaseline decision date: 2029-08-05 (previously 2029-07-22). MAP v3 updated accordingly.
2) Backstop: If acceptance not achieved by 2029-08-05, Redwood will issue a one-time credit equal to 7.5% of the first full invoice or provide 30 days of service credit (BrightHealth to choose). Credit capped as outlined in the amendment.
3) Evidence exchange: BrightHealth to transmit SOC-2 excerpts and procurement checklist by 2029-07-18 EOD. Redwood to surface any required instance-level logs within 2 business days of request.
4) Contingency: If security blocks production access, we will proceed with a staged sandbox review (no traffic) and hold billing until acceptance gating is satisfied.

Next steps (for closure):
- Jordan/legal to push the amendment (signed DocuSign link below).
- Alex/procurement: confirm which backstop remedy you prefer (credit vs. usage credit) by 2029-07-18.
- Karthik: please attach the SOC excerpts and the short artifacts pack to the HubSpot record once available.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/templates/BH-1245-MAP
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/1245
